svg.title: Contract the Model, Then Clear the Trip-Wires
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-commercial-guardrail-roadmap; chapter number: 12; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Contract the Model, Then Clear the Trip-Wires; subtitle: Hybrid pricing and financial-sector guardrails; caption: Recurring, risk-shared revenue wins, but finance clients bring hard regulatory trip-wires that have to be cleared on time.; assumptions note: Week sequencing is an ordering convention; practitioners did not prescribe week-by-week timing. Regulatory thresholds are as quoted by the named channels.; note: Sources - Rafael Hernandez (XPcFTfp7i8E), Centimillionaire Strategies (N8Z0FPf2yLw), Financial Regulation Courses (CmOezPFI5ew), All Things SPVs (F1OsgcF_bhg).; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Contract the Hybrid Retainer; deliverable: Contract covering ad-spend funding, ad and pixel ownership, the paid-result definition, the fifty-fifty resale split, and credit pricing and expiry.; gate: Retainer cut from roughly $5K to $2K a month, with pay per delivered result (Rafael Hernandez).; week: Week 2; title: Lock Introductions; deliverable: Non-circumvention clauses on every introduction.; gate: No large allocation from an investor who has never met the manager in person (Centimillionaire Strategies).; week: Week 3; title: Retail Communication Check; deliverable: Recipient count per piece, with no sales contests or quotas under Reg BI.; gate: More than 25 retail investors in any 30-calendar-day period requires principal pre-approval (Financial Regulation Courses).; week: Week 4; title: File Form D and Blue Skies; deliverable: Form D with the date of first sale set to the countersigned close.; gate: Filed within 15 days of the close (All Things SPVs).
